newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says Cuba has "lost its luster" for rebels.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says Cuba has "lost its luster" for rebels.

text.p: State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns on Tuesday mocked Cuba, suggesting it had "lost a little bit of its luster in revolutionary circles" because Peru's Tupac Amaru rebels were cool to seeking asylum there.

"I think that's a commentary on the state of affairs in Cuba today. Maybe Cuba has lost a little bit of its luster in revolutionary circles," he said, underscoring long-standing U.S. antipathy for Castro and his communist rule in Cuba.

The Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) -- a group of Marxist rebels holding 72 hostages in Lima, Peru -- on Tuesday poured cold water on a proposal to win them asylum abroad in return for a peaceful end to the 77-day crisis.
Their leader insisted the rebels want to stay in Peru and urged the government to concentrate instead on their principal demand for the freedom of some 400 jailed comrades.
Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori Monday diverted his executive jet to Cuba for talks with Castro. He later said the Cuban leader had agreed conditionally to give asylum to the Peruvian rebels.
